## Oklahoma

Long before Oklahoma achieved statehood, Native nations and territorial governments had established laws governing the carrying and use of firearms. Restrictions on concealed weapons, public discharge, and dueling reflected a broader tradition of maintaining public order amid rapid settlement and social change.

#### State: Oklahoma

Level Of Government: State 

Jurisdiction Covered: State of Oklahoma 

Year: 1910 

Regulation Type: Sentence Enhancement 

Regulation Target:

Origin: Code 

 Description

This law criminalizes rioting. It also establishes that carrying a firearm or other deadly weapon while rioting is punishable by imprisonment for between 2 and 10 years. This is a republication of the riot law in the 1908 code.

Citation

Revised Laws of Oklahoma (St. Paul: The Pioneer Co., 1912), 630-631, §2559.

Level Of Government: State 

Jurisdiction Covered: State of Oklahoma 

Year: 1910 

This law establishes that breaking and entering a home with a weapon is to be classified as burglary in the first degree if done in the nighttime or as burglary in the second degree if done in the daytime. Punishment for burglary in the first degree includes imprisonment for between 7 and 20 years; for burglary in the second degree, it includes imprisonment for between 2 and 7 years. This is a republication of the armed burglary law in the 1908 code.

Revised Laws of Oklahoma (St. Paul: The Pioneer Co., 1912), 639, §2611.

Year: 1910 

This law establishes that “intentionally and wrongfully” shooting, shooting at, or attempting to shoot another person with intent to kill is punishable by imprisonment for up to 10 years. This is a republication of the shooting with intent law in the 1908 code in slightly different language.

Revised Laws of Oklahoma (St. Paul: The Pioneer Co., 1912), 581, §2336.

Year: 1910 

This law establishes that assault with a dangerous weapon, a criminal category which includes attempting to shoot another person without intent to kill, is punishable by imprisonment for up to 5 years in the penitentiary or up to 1 year in a county jail. This is a republication of the assault with a dangerous weapon law in the 1908 code in slightly different language.

Revised Laws of Oklahoma (St. Paul: The Pioneer Co., 1912), 584, §2344.

### 1884: Carry – Chickasaw Nation

Jurisdiction Covered: Chickasaw Nation 

Year: 1884 

This law prohibits the carrying of handguns within Chickasaw Nation territory. Law enforcement is excepted. Punishment includes a fine of between $25 and $100, and imprisonment for between 1 and 3 months if the fine cannot be paid.

“An act to prohibit the carrying of pistols within the limits of the Chickasaw Nation,” General and Special Laws of the Chickasaw Nation, Passed during the Sessions of the Legislature from the Years 1878 to 1884, Inclusive (Muskogee: Indian Journal Steam Job Print, 1884), 58-59.

### 1893: Sensitive Places | Carry – Muscogee Creek Nation

Jurisdiction Covered: Muscogee Creek Nation 

Year: 1893 

Regulation Type: Carry, Sensitive Places 

This law prohibits the carrying of deadly weapons within half a mile of town or at any “political or religious or other gathering, for pleasure or profit” as well as the discharge of firearms “at random within one-half mile of any town or gathering as above mentioned.” Punishment includes forfeit of the weapon as well as a fine of $10, or $50 if the weapon is concealed. No property is to be exempted from seizure for the settlement of this fine. Exceptions are made for travelers, public officers, and people hunting stock.

Constitution and Laws of the Muskogee Nation, as Compiled and Codified by A.P. McKellop, Under Act of October 15, 1892 (Muskogee, Indian Territory: F.C. Hubbard, 1893), 61-62, §§161-166.

### 1893: Sensitive Places | Carry – Muscogee Creek Nation

Jurisdiction Covered: Muscogee Creek Nation 

Year: 1893 

This law prohibits the arrest of any member of the Muscogee Creek Nation at an election unless for breaching the peace or carrying a deadly weapon. This is a reproduction of the 1880 law governing election arrests in slightly different language.

Constitution and Laws of the Muskogee Nation, as Compiled and Codified by A.P. McKellop, Under Act of October 15, 1892 (Muskogee, Indian Territory: F.C. Hubbard, 1893), 50-51, §122.
